check_results.observed: capacitor_voltage_V maximum is 10 V and minimum is -7.28036 V over the full reported run, so |capacitor_voltage_V| exceeds 0.3 V. The merged evaluable form applied this as an always-over-full-run check, not a bounded 50 s to 150 s window. Expected |capacitor_voltage_V| <= 0.3 always under that merged check form.

summary: The simulated run clearly shows the intended underdamped RLC discharge after the switch closes: switch_closed stays 0 until t=5.000000001000071 s, then changes to 1 once and remains closed; capacitor_voltage_V swings negative to a minimum of -7.28036 V and settles to 2.58751e-06 V by 150 s, while loop_current_A settles to -2.15825e-06 A by 150 s. However, this run is not fully valid against the stated acceptance set as supplied here because three checks cannot be evaluated from the provided result data alone: capacitor_voltage_V at t=4 s, loop_current_A at t=4 s, and |loop_current_A| at t=8.16 s are not given as time-stamped values. In addition, the merged AC-08 formulation fails when applied as an always-over-full-run condition, because the voltage reaches 10 V initially and -7.28036 V later, both larger than 0.3 V in magnitude.
issues: AC-02 capacitor voltage at 4 s is not evaluable from the supplied data: capacitor_voltage_V is reported only by min/max/final, with no value at t=4.0 s.
AC-02 loop current at 4 s is not evaluable from the supplied data: loop_current_A is reported only by min/max/final, with no value at t=4.0 s.
AC-05 loop current near zero at 8.16 s is not evaluable from the supplied data: loop_current_A is reported only by min/max/final, with no value at t=8.16 s.

AC-08 fails under the merged evaluable form because it was applied as an always-over-full-run condition: |capacitor_voltage_V| reaches 10 V initially and 7.28036 V at negative overshoot, both greater than the 0.3 V limit.
assumptions: For AC-08, the original requirement was |capacitor_voltage_V| <= 0.3 V over t = 50 s to 150 s, but the merged check applied it as an always condition over the full run because the schema could not represent a bounded time window.
For AC-02, the original combined absolute tolerance 0.01 at t = 4 s was split and applied separately to capacitor_voltage_V and loop_current_A.
No solver tolerance was specified in the brief; the model used Interval = 0.15 s to produce 1000 intervals over 150 s.
The capacitor negative pin was connected to ground as the single electrical reference so the network is structurally solvable.
The ideal switch was modeled with Ron = 1e-6 Ohm and Goff = 1e-6 S because the brief did not specify non-ideal switch parameters.
switch_closed was implemented as a Real-valued 0/1 reported signal while the internal switch command remained Boolean.
The stated damping ratio 0.1 and natural frequency 1 rad/s were retained for traceability but not used as independent governing inputs; the run is determined by R = 0.2 Ohm, L = 1 H, and C = 1 F.

A further model-implied assumption is that the pre-charge is represented as an initial capacitor voltage of 10 V with no active source in the circuit after t = 0, so all subsequent energy in the run comes from the initially stored capacitor energy and then decays through the resistor.
root_causes: The three not-evaluable checks are a reporting/data-availability problem, not a demonstrated trajectory failure: the supplied evidence contains only min/max/final summaries for continuous variables plus discrete-event changes, so exact values of capacitor_voltage_V and loop_current_A at t = 4.0 s and of loop_current_A at t = 8.16 s cannot be read from the provided data.

AC-08 fails because of the merged check formulation, not because the physical run failed to settle late in time. The actual model starts with the capacitor pre-charged to 10 V and then, after the switch closes at about 5 s, produces underdamped ringing down to -7.28036 V before decaying toward zero. Those intended early-time behaviors necessarily violate an always-over-full-run limit of |capacitor_voltage_V| <= 0.3 V. The conflict comes from replacing the original bounded late-time window t = 50 s to 150 s with a full-run always condition.
